newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: PRESS DIGEST - Bangladesh Newspapers - Sept 30.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Bangladesh Newspapers - Sept 30.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Bangladesh press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

Bangladesh's Finance Minister S A M S Kibria has called upon donor countries to maintain adequate flow of official assistance needed for poverty reduction and infrastructure development. "Private flow cannot be a substitute for official flows," he told reporters in Washington at the end of the Commonwealth Finance Minister's conference.
Tribal insurgents in Chittagong hill districts have unilaterally announced extension of the truce till October 31. The on-going ceasefire is due to expire on Monday (today).

Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina has said her government decided to make parliament the centre of all nation building activities. "We will discuss all national problems in the parliament where we will take all the major decisions," she said while launching a task force to strengthen the support services at the parliament secretariat.

Jute, one of the country's main cash crops, is selling between Tk 275 and 350 ($6.5-8.5) per maund in local market, down from last year's price level. Market sources said price was lower because of the absence of adequate buyers.
Commerce and Industry Minister Tofael Ahmed said the government was stressing on rapid industrialisation to attain an economic growth of at least seven percent in next one year.
